Hi Dana,

Thanks — listing the defaults and options below so you can paste answers into the questionnaire. I'll attach SOC2 and our erase runbook in a follow-up.

Short answers (hosted API defaults):
- Raw prompt (user input): stored by default for 30 days. This includes the full request payload and associated request metadata (time, client id, model version).
- Streamed fragments / intermediate buffers: treated as ephemeral; we persist streaming fragments only until session finalization and they are retained at most 24 hours unless the session is marked for longer retention for debugging.
- Final completion(s) (model outputs): retained by default for 90 days for billing reconciliation and quality monitoring.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranker scores, traces): defaults vary by artifact: embeddings are retained 90 days; evaluation traces/latency logs are retained 180 days.

Residency:
- Hosted requests routed to a regional cluster keep data in-region by default (US/EU/APAC). If your tenant is configured for EU residency we'll keep stored artifacts in EU regions.
- Dedicated or Private deployments give you full control of residency and storage; for PHI we typically recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) where you control the storage backend and KMS.

Erasure / proof-of-deletion:
- Standard erasure request timeline (hosted): we acknowledge within 24 hours and complete the deletion from active stores within 72 hours.
- Proof provided: a deletion certificate that includes object ids removed, timestamps, and the storage locations cleared (we can provide redacted evidence suitable for your auditors).
- Note: for backups and archival tiers there is an additional purge pipeline; we include those records and timestamps in the deletion certificate once background purge completes (usually within 7–21 days depending on retention windows).

Options and controls to change defaults:
1) Retention overrides: we can set tenant-level retention (shorten to 0 days for prompts, or extend/reduce other buckets) for Hosted pilots via a configuration flag — requires an admin request and change control.
2) Disable-capture mode: option to run requests in "no-store" mode (prompts not persisted) — this blocks many platform features (billing by token still works via ephemeral metering).
3) Private deployment: recommended for regulated PHI workloads — schedule varies (4–8 weeks typical depending on network and compliance onboarding).

I'll attach SOC2 and the erasure runbook in the next message. If you want, we can also provide a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for a PHI pilot that lists the controls and timings.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of compliance notes from procurement/security coordination side:

- EU residency: when a tenant is configured for EU-only storage we ensure all persisted artifacts (prompts, outputs, embeddings) remain on EU-hosted storage and don't cross regions. Audit logs will show regional data plane selection.
- Billing and debugging logs: by default, request-level billing metadata (token counts, timestamp, record id) is available for 90 days — if you need a shorter window we can contractually cap that.
- DPA & SCP: I can circulate a DPA redline and our standard Security Control Pack for Health (we include encryption-at-rest details, key rotation cadence, and SOC2 redactions).

For PHI specifically, we usually recommend: 1) Private deployment, 2) Customer-managed KMS, 3) Explicit data processing addendum signed before pilot.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
